memory_update.text: Add MU as the highest-confidence US-listed direct HBM supplier for the hbm_memory_advanced_packaging node.
Add ONTO as a less-obvious HBM4 inspection/metrology equipment candidate with direct company-disclosed HBM manufacturer selection evidence.
Add TER and FORM as HBM test/probe-card equipment candidates; these may benefit if known-good-die, stack validation, and advanced-package test become gating factors.
Add ASX as a US-listed ADR candidate for advanced packaging and HBM/chiplet heterogeneous integration exposure.
SK hynix and Samsung are central HBM suppliers but were not added to the candidate list because this pass prioritizes US-listed exchange-traded companies; track separately as non-US or OTC coverage.

HBM allocation should be tracked as a multi-node constraint spanning memory wafer starts, advanced packaging capacity, HBM stack yield, probe cards, inspection/metrology, and automated test equipment.

node: HBM, advanced DRAM allocation, and advanced packaging capacity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the HBM and advanced-packaging allocation chokepoint. The strongest directly mapped candidates are Micron for HBM supply, ASE Technology for advanced packaging and HBM/chiplet integration exposure, Teradyne and FormFactor for HBM test/probe bottlenecks, and Onto Innovation for HBM4 inspection/metrology. This pass excludes non-US-exchange leaders such as SK hynix and Samsung from the candidate list despite their central role, creating an explicit coverage gap.
